data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"No single mechanism explains the nocturnal UHI or its cross-city variation: the phenomenon emerges from the interaction of thermal mass, sky view factor, anthropogenic heat, and evapotranspiration, and the dominant cross-city modulator depends on the climate regime. In arid cities the dominant modulator is vegetation and irrigation; in dense temperate cities it is sky view factor and thermal mass; in high-latitude cities it is anthropogenic heat. In arid climates evapotranspiration differences dominate because the countryside is dry; in dense temperate cities radiative geometry dominates; in cold cities anthropogenic heat dominates.
